outcome: Intraoperative complications (excessive blood loss, bladder injury, bowel injury, ureteric injury, conversion to TAH)
Postoperative complications (vault infection, subacute intestinal obstruction, VVF, RVF, stress urinary incontinence, vault prolapse, vault cellulitis)
cohort: The study included 105 patients who underwent vaginal hysterectomy, with the majority (69%) being between 40-49 years of age.
finding: Vaginal hysterectomy was associated with low intraoperative and postoperative complications, quicker recovery, shorter hospitalization, and early discharge.
